stem: Find the area bounded by the curve \(y = x^2\), the Y axis, the X axis and \(x = 3\).
solution:
The required area \(A = \int_{x=0}^{3} y\,dx\)
\(A = \int_{0}^{3} x^2\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{3}\)
\(A = 9 - 0 = 9\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the region bounded by the curves \(y^2 = 9x\) and \(x^2 = 9y\).
solution:
The equations of the curves are
\(y^2 = 9x\) ..... (I)
and \(x^2 = 9y\) ..... (II)
Squaring equation (II),
\(x^4 = 81y^2\)
\(x^4 = 81(9x)\) ... by (I)
\(x^4 = 729x\)
\(\therefore x(x^3 - 9^3) = 0\)
i.e. \(x(x^3 - 9^3) = 0\)
\(\Rightarrow x = 0\) or \(x = 9\)
From equation (II), \(y = 0\) or \(y = 9\)
\(\therefore\) The points of intersection of the curves are \((0, 0), (9, 9)\).
\(\therefore\) Required area \(A = \int_{0}^{9} \sqrt{9x}\,dx - \int_{0}^{9} \dfrac{x^2}{9}\,dx\)
\(= \left[3 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot x^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{9} - \left[\dfrac{1}{9} \cdot \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{9}\)
\(= 2 \cdot 9^{3/2} - 27\)
\(A = 54 - 27 = 27\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area bounded by the curve \(y = -x^2\), X-axis and lines \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\).
solution:
Let A be the area bounded by the curve \(y = -x^2\), X-axis and \(1 \le x \le 4\).
The required area \(A = \int_{1}^{4} y\,dx = \int_{1}^{4} -x^2\,dx = \left[-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{1}^{4} = -\dfrac{64}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\)
\(A = -21\),
But we consider the area to be positive.
\(\therefore A = |-21| = 21\) square units.
Thus, if \(f(x) \le 0\) or \(f(x) \ge 0\) in \([a, b]\) then the area enclosed between \(y = f(x)\), X-axis and \(x = a, x = b\) is \(\left|\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx\right|\).

stem: Find the area bounded by the line \(y = x\), X axis and the lines \(x = -1\) and \(x = 4\).
solution:
Consider the area A, bounded by straight line \(y = x\), X axis and \(x = -1, x = 4\).
From the figure, A is divided into \(A_1\) and \(A_2\).
The required area \(A_1 = \int_{-1}^{0} y\,dx = \int_{-1}^{0} x\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-1}^{0} = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(A_1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}\) square units.
But area is always positive.
\(\therefore A_1 = \left|-\dfrac{1}{2}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}\) square units.
\(A_2 = \int_{0}^{4} y\,dx = \int_{0}^{4} x\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{4} = \dfrac{4^2}{2} = 8\) square units.
\(\therefore\) Required area \(A = A_1 + A_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} + 8 = \dfrac{17}{2}\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area enclosed between the X-axis and the curve \(y = \sin x\) for values of \(x\) between 0 to \(2\pi\).
solution:
The area enclosed between the curve and the X-axis consists of equal area lying alternatively above and below X-axis which are respectively positive and negative.
1) Area \(A_1 = \) area lying above the X-axis \(= \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x\,dx = \left[-\cos x\right]_{0}^{\pi} = -[\cos \pi - \cos 0] = -(-1 - 1)\)
\(A_1 = 2\)
2) Area \(A_2 = \) area lying below the X-axis \(= \int_{\pi}^{2\pi} \sin x\,dx = \left[-\cos x\right]_{\pi}^{2\pi} = -[\cos 2\pi - \cos \pi] = -[1 - (-1)]\)
\(A_2 = -2\)
\(\therefore\) Total area \(= A_1 + |A_2| = 2 + |(-2)| = 4\) sq. units.

stem: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the line \(2y + x = 8\), X-axis and the lines \(x = 2\) and \(x = 4\).
solution:
The required region is bounded by the lines \(2y + x = 8\), and \(x = 2, x = 4\) and X-axis.
\(\therefore y = \dfrac{1}{2}(8 - x)\) and the limits are \(x = 2, x = 4\).
Required area \(= \) Area of the shaded region
\(= \int_{x=2}^{4} y\,dx = \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{1}{2}(8 - x)\,dx\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[8x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_{2}^{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\left(8 \cdot 4 - \dfrac{4^2}{2}\right) - \left(8 \cdot 2 - \dfrac{2^2}{2}\right)\right]\)
\(= 5\) sq. units.

stem:
Find the area of the regions bounded by the following curve, the X-axis and the given lines:
(i) \(y = x^2\), \(x = 1\), \(x = 2\)
(ii) \(y^2 = 4x\), \(x = 1\), \(x = 4\), \(y \ge 0\)
(iii) \(y = \sin x\), \(x = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
solution:
Let A be the required area.
(i) \(A = \int_{1}^{3} y\,dx = \int_{1}^{3} x^2\,dx = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[x^3\right]_{1}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}[27 - 1]\), \(A = \dfrac{26}{3}\) sq. units.
(ii) \(A = \int_{1}^{4} y\,dx = \int_{1}^{4} 2\sqrt{x}\,dx = 2\int_{1}^{4} x^{1/2}\,dx = 2 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_{1}^{4} = \dfrac{4}{3}\left[4^{3/2} - 1\right]\), \(A = \dfrac{28}{3}\) sq. units.
(iii) \(A = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} y\,dx = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \sin x\,dx = \left|\int_{-\pi/2}^{0} \sin x\,dx\right| + \left|\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\,dx\right| = \left|\left[-\cos x\right]_{-\pi/2}^{0}\right| + \left|\left[-\cos x\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\right| = \left|-\left[\cos 0 - \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]\right| + \left|\left[-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + \cos 0\right]\right| = |[-1 - 0]| + |[0 + 1]| = 1 + 1\), \(A = 2\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola \(y^2 = 16x\) and the line \(x = 4\).
solution:
\(y^2 = 16x \Rightarrow y = \pm 4\sqrt{x}\)
\(A = \) Area POCP \(+\) Area QOCQ
\(= 2\,(\text{Area POCP})\)
\(= 2\int_{0}^{4} y\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{4} 4\sqrt{x}\,dx\)
\(A = 8 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\left[x^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{4} = \dfrac{16}{3} \times 8\)
\(A = \dfrac{128}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the region bounded by the curves \(x^2 = 16y\), \(y = 1\), \(y = 4\) and the Y-axis, lying in the first quadrant.
solution:
Required area \(= \int_{1}^{4} x\,dy\)
\(A = \int_{1}^{4} \sqrt{16y}\,dy = 4\int_{1}^{4} \sqrt{y}\,dy = 4 \cdot \left[\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot y^{3/2}\right]_{1}^{4} = \dfrac{8}{3} \times [8 - 1]\)
\(A = \dfrac{56}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\).
solution:
By the symmetry of the ellipse, required area of the ellipse is 4 times the area of the region OPQO. For this region the limit of integration are \(x = 0\) and \(x = a\).
From the equation of ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\)
\(\dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1 - \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}\)
\(y^2 = b^2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{a^2 - x^2}{a^2}\right)\)
\(y = \dfrac{b}{a} \cdot \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\), In first quadrant, \(y > 0\)
\(A = 4\int_{x=0}^{a} y\,dx = 4\int_{0}^{a} \dfrac{b}{a} \cdot \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx\)
\(= \dfrac{4b}{a} \cdot \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\right]_{0}^{a}\)
\(= \dfrac{4b}{a} \cdot \left[\dfrac{a^2}{2} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0\right]\)
\(A = \pi a b\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the region lying between the parabolas \(y^2 = 4ax\) and \(x^2 = 4ay\) where \(a > 0\).
solution:
The equations of the parabolas are
\(y^2 = 4ax\) ... (I)
and \(x^2 = 4ay\) ... (II)
From (II) \(y = \dfrac{x^2}{4a}\) substitute in (I)
\(\left(\dfrac{x^2}{4a}\right)^2 = 4ax\)
\(\Rightarrow x^4 = 64a^3 x\)
\(\therefore x(x^3 - 64a^3) = 0\)
\(\therefore x[x^3 - (4a)^3] = 0\)
\(\therefore x = 0\) and \(x = 4a\) \(\therefore y = 0\) and \(y = 4a\)
The point of intersection of curves are \(O(0, 0)\), \(P(4a, 4a)\)
\(\therefore\) The required area is in the first quadrant and it is
A \(= \) area under the parabola (\(y^2 = 4ax\)) \(- \) area under the parabola (\(x^2 = 4ay\))
\(A = \int_{0}^{4a} \sqrt{4ax}\,dx - \int_{0}^{4a} \dfrac{x^2}{4a}\,dx = \sqrt{4a}\int_{0}^{4a} x^{1/2}\,dx - \int_{0}^{4a} \dfrac{x^2}{4a}\,dx\)
\(= 2\sqrt{a} \cdot \left[\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot x^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{4a} - \dfrac{1}{4a} \cdot \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{4a}\)
\(= \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{a} \cdot \left[4a\sqrt{4a}\right] - \dfrac{1}{4a} \cdot 64a^3 = \dfrac{32}{3}a^2 - \dfrac{16}{3}a^2\)
\(\therefore A = \dfrac{16}{3}a^2\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve \(y = x^2\) and the line \(y = 4\).
solution:
Required area \(A = 2 \times\) area of OPQO
\(\therefore A = \int_{0}^{4} x \cdot dy\)
\(A = 2 \cdot \int_{0}^{4} \sqrt{y} \cdot dy = 2 \cdot \left[\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot y^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{4} = \left(\dfrac{4}{3} \times 4^{3/2}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times 8\)
\(A = \dfrac{32}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of sector bounded by the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 16\) and the line \(y = x\) in the first quadrant.
solution:
Required area \(A = A(\triangle OCB) + A(\text{region ABC})\)
To find, the point of intersection of \(x^2 + y^2 = 16\) ... (I) and line \(y = x\) ... (II)
Substitute (II) in (I)
\(x^2 + x^2 = 16\)
\(2x^2 = 16\)
\(x^2 = 8\)
\(x = \pm 2\sqrt{2}\), \(y = \pm 2\sqrt{2}\)
The point of intersection is \(B(2\sqrt{2}, 2\sqrt{2})\)
\(A = \int_{0}^{2\sqrt{2}} x\,dx + \int_{2\sqrt{2}}^{4} \sqrt{16 - x^2}\,dx\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x^2\right]_{0}^{2\sqrt{2}} + \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + \dfrac{16}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_{2\sqrt{2}}^{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot (2\sqrt{2})^2 + \left[8\sin^{-1}1 - \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{8} + 8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)\right]\)
\(= 4 + 8 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 4 - 8 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
\(\therefore A = 2\pi\) sq. units.
Note that, the required area is \(\dfrac{1}{8}\) times the area of the circle given.
